stated: The Conservative Party will reform the Child Maintenance Service to prevent non-compliance and introduce new laws to crack down on non-payment, while also improving support for victims of domestic or economic abuse.

source.quote: We will reform the Child Maintenance Service to prevent noncompliance and new laws to help crack down on non-payment. We’ll also look at how the Service can better support victims of domestic or economic abuse...

bearing_set.reason: Enforcing child maintenance payment directly increases real disposable income for single-parent (predominantly mother-headed) households, materially affecting their ability to afford essentials.

The policy explicitly targets domestic and economic abuse victims through CMS reform, and introduces new enforcement laws — both the safety dimension for abuse victims and the justice-system mechanism (new legislation, compliance enforcement) fall within O5's scope.

Single-parent families face markedly higher poverty rates; better enforcement transfers income from typically higher-earning non-resident parents to lower-earning primary carers, plausibly narrowing the household income gap and reducing child poverty.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: a direct income-for-essentials effect on one of the most financially vulnerable household types (O2), an explicit domestic/economic abuse protection element using justice-system powers (O5), and a distributional effect narrowing the income gap for children in single-parent households (O14). These are distinct rather than overlapping.
